newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen opening steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen opening steady to lower.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open steady to lower Wednesday following a strong rally Tuesday on the final day of trade for the June contract, industry sources said.
Early over the counter talk for the July contract was thin and covered wide ranges, the sources said.
"Most people are still taking care of June, July talk has been very quiet so far this morning," said one New York based futures trader.
July Palo Verde (PV) was pegged at $30.50-31.50 in early over the counter discussion from Tuesday's NYMEX July futures close at $31.22 per megawatt hour (MWh).
July California Oregon Border (COB) was talked over the counter at $22.00-23.00 from Tuesday's close at $23.11 per MWh.
NYMEX electricity futures ralled strongly Tuesday on news of an unexpected outage at the 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit in Arizona.
Arizona Public Service said it expects to restore output from the unit on Wednesday. Palo Verde 1 was in a hot standby mode as of early Wednesday, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said.
Tuesday was the final day of trade for the June electricity contracts.
Talk of the outage combined with some short positions Tuesday also pushed physical power prices strongly higher.
July NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures opened down about 1.6 cents at near $2.345 per million British thermal units.
In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be near or just below normal through the week, then rising to four to eight degrees above normal on the weekend.
In Seattle, temperatures were expected to reach a maximum o 67 degrees Fahrenheit Thursday, with a low near 51 degrees.

In the Southwest, temperatures were expected to be three to seven degrees above normal through into the early weekend across the extreme south and west. To the north and east, temperatures were expected to be near to slightly above normal through into the weekend.
In Phoenix, Ariz., temperatures were expected to reach a maximum near 96 degrees Wednesday with lows expected near 70 degrees.

A total of about 7,000 megawatts of power generation remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance. However, much of the idled generation was expected to return to service over the next several weeks.
The 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit was expected to begin production May 29 from a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began April 19.
Several coal-fired plants were also expected back at the end of month, including the 750 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and 750 MW Four Corners unit in Arizona.
